items.title: Prof. John Amuasi calls for a shift towards preventing health crises at World Health Summit
items.description: Professor John H. Amuasi of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi (KNUST), has called for a shift in how countries approach public health, urging governments to address the conditions that make people sick rather than focusing largely on treating diseases after they occur. Speaking at the World Health Summit 2026 in Berlin, Germany, Prof. Amuasi said building stronger health systems would require greater attention to environmental, social and economic factors that put populations at risk. His presentation, “One Health and Upstream Prevention”, formed part of a session titled “Ecological Determinants of Resilient Health Systems: Scaling Upstream Prevention to Anticipate, Prevent, and Adapt to Emerging Health Risks.” Prof. Amuasi, who is also Co-Chair of The Lancet One Health Commission, used the example of people falling into a river to explain why health systems must pay greater attention to prevention. He likened conventional healthcare responses to rescuing people who have already fallen into the water. While such interventions are necessary and save lives, he explained that it is equally important to find out why people keep falling in and prevent it from happening. The approach, known as upstream prevention , focuses on addressing the underlying causes of poor health before they result in disease or other health emergencies. For Prof. Amuasi, achieving this requires a better understanding of the relationship between human health, animal health and the shared environment. Drawing on the work of the Lancet One Health Commission, he explained that health cannot be considered in isolation from the natural and social environments in which people live. He highlighted how climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss and human activities affect health in ways that often extend beyond national borders and individual communities. The One Health approach, he noted, provides a way to understand these connections and develop solutions that involve sectors beyond healthcare. Using examples familiar to Ghana, Prof. Amuasi pointed to illegal mining, food safety and environmental pollution as issues that demonstrate why prevention must begin outside hospitals and health facilities. He drew attention to the effects of environmentally destructive mining activities on water, soil and air, as well as questions about the safety and quality of food produced or sold under different environmental and regulatory conditions. He also raised concerns about exposure to polluted air and the environmental implications of plastic packaging, highlighting how everyday decisions and economic activities can have consequences for health. These challenges, he indicated, cannot be addressed by the health sector alone but require coordinated efforts involving environmental authorities, agriculture, education, industry and policymakers. Beyond policy and environmental interventions, Prof. Amuasi placed particular emphasis on education and the need to change how people think about health. He argued that introducing One Health concepts early in the educational system could gradually shape how future generations understand their responsibilities towards people, animals and the environment. “If we are able to change the way people think about health and help them understand the fundamental interconnectedness of humans, animals and our shared environment, beginning at the earliest levels of education, from primary school through secondary school to university, I believe that in a decade or more, we will begin to reap the benefits,” he said. He explained that this would help people appreciate the One Health concept regardless of their academic backgrounds or professional disciplines. “This understanding can influence value systems, even as those values differ across societies and cultures,” he added. Prof. Amuasi also highlighted the role of the media and other communication platforms in shaping public understanding of health and environmental issues. He called for closer collaboration between scientists, educators and media professionals to ensure that information about health and the environment reaches people in ways they can understand and apply in their daily lives. The presentation drew on the work of The Lancet One Health Commission, which advocates a broader understanding of health that considers the interconnected relationships between humans, animals, plants and the environment. The Commission’s framework places emphasis on equity, sustainability, systems thinking and the need to recognise different forms of knowledge when developing health policies. According to Prof. Amuasi’s message, while countries must continue investing in hospitals, medicines and emergency response systems, greater attention must also be given to preventing the conditions that lead to illness.

items.title: ECG’s billing adjustments: consumers feel robbed, PURC must intervene
items.description: An electricity bill should explain what a customer owes. When thousands of cedis appear under the word “adjustment”, without a clear account of how the amount was calculated, that bill becomes a demand for trust the supplier has done little to earn. That is the anger running through complaints about the Electricity Company of Ghana’s postpaid billing. One customer reports a GH¢9,000 adjustment. Another says an adjustment increased a bill from GH¢90 to GH¢1,189. Others ask what happens to people who have already paid amounts subsequently found to be excessive. There are also complaints of customers trooping daily to ECG’s Kumasi Substation offices, its Hohoe office and offices in parts of Accra, seeking explanations for disputed bills. They describe encounters with tellers and other frontline staff whose responses they consider dismissive, unreasonable and unhelpful. These accounts require investigation, including examination of the underlying bills and ECG’s responses. They do not, by themselves, establish deliberate theft. But they raise questions that cannot be answered by sending frustrated consumers from one counter to another. A person who takes time off work, spends money on transport and joins a queue to challenge a bill deserves a patient hearing and an intelligible explanation. Where a teller cannot resolve the matter, there should be a clear route to someone who can. The customer should leave with a complaint reference, a responsible officer and a timeframe for a response. Poor customer service adds humiliation to financial distress. An employee may not have created a billing error, but treating the person affected with contempt compounds the institution’s failure. Courtesy, competence and accountability are basic requirements of public service. For a household budgeting carefully for food, rent and school fees, a large unexplained adjustment is a financial shock. Calling it a technical correction does not make the money easier to find. The problem has a documented history. In November 2023, ECG acknowledged that a new process had caused difficulties with estimated bills. Its “fix the bill, pay the bill” exercise involved taking and verifying actual meter readings to produce accurate bills. Billing failures therefore cannot simply be dismissed as customers misunderstanding their consumption. An adjustment can be legitimate. If earlier bills underestimated actual consumption, a subsequent reading may reveal a shortfall. Paying every bill received does not necessarily mean every unit consumed has been fully charged. But ECG must demonstrate that shortfall. The word “adjustment” proves nothing by itself. A proper explanation should identify the period being corrected, the relevant meter readings, the units previously billed, the applicable tariffs and all payments already received. It should show how the revised balance was reached. A customer should be able to follow the calculation without needing an acquaintance inside the company. Where data migration or a system change is offered as an explanation, ECG should provide the records connecting the old balance to the new one. People designed the system, entered its data and authorised its use. People must answer for its mistakes. That responsibility extends to the boardroom. ECG’s board and its management, headed by Ing. Julius Kwame Kpekpena, must explain what safeguards protect customers from incorrect adjustments and how those safeguards are monitored. What is the value of assembling experienced professionals around a boardroom table if an ordinary customer still cannot obtain a clear explanation of a debt? When the board considers revenue collection, does it demand evidence that the amounts being pursued are accurate? Does it examine how disputed bills are handled, how customers are treated and how quickly errors are corrected? These are questions of judgment and conscience as much as administration. Any discussion of recovering thousands of cedis from a struggling household should include a simple question: can we demonstrate, clearly and fairly, that this money is owed? A responsible board should require that answer before endorsing collection procedures. It should insist that management bring the experience at the customer-service counter into its assessment of corporate performance. Revenue figures alone cannot tell the full story of an institution entrusted with an essential service. Ghana’s consumer-service regulations already recognise the need for safeguards. Regulation 33 of L.I. 2413 requires a utility recovering an undercharge to inform the consumer and offer an instalment payment option. Regulation 32 requires disputed bills to be reviewed and reconciled, while consumers remain responsible for the undisputed portion. These protections should be visible in everyday dealings with ECG. The threat of losing electricity must never become a substitute for explaining a bill. The question of money already collected is equally urgent. A customer who borrowed to settle an inflated bill has lost access to money needed elsewhere. An apology cannot replenish the family budget. Regulation 34 requires utilities to correct overcharges promptly, credit the consumer’s account with the full excess amount and notify the consumer. It also provides for interest, at a rate determined by PURC, where overcharging continues for three months or more. Once ECG identifies a common billing error, it should proactively review every affected account. Corrections should reach customers who paid quietly, struggled with the complaints process or never realised something was wrong. PURC should require a public accounting of the accounts examined, incorrect charges identified, amounts reversed, credits issued and complaints still unresolved. Independent checks should establish whether failures arose from faulty readings, software, poor supervision or deliberate misconduct. Where wrongdoing is established, responsibility must reach those who caused or permitted it. Some consumers describe their experience as “professional” robbery. That language conveys the helplessness of being asked to surrender money to an institution whose calculations they cannot inspect. ECG should take that distrust seriously. Every cedi demanded must be accounted for. Every customer questioning a bill deserves respect. Every established overcharge must be corrected. The board and management should make those standards the test of their leadership. A household’s poverty must never become the reason its questions go unanswered.

items.title: URGENT : Tous les candidats au poste de chef de l’ONU essuient un veto lors d’un vote (diplomate)
items.description: Tous les candidats au poste de secrétaire général de l'ONU se sont vu vendredi opposer un avis négatif de membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité, qui disposent d'un droit de veto, lors d'un vote de cette instance, a-t-on appris de source diplomatique. Au terme de ce vote qui n'est encore qu'indicatif, aucun des sept candidats n'a réussi à échapper à un vote négatif des cinq grandes puissances – Grande-Bretagne, France, États-Unis, Chine et Russie –, ce qui ouvre la voie à de probables nouvelles candidatures. Quatre femmes et trois hommes tentent à ce jour de succéder au Portugais António Guterres, 77 ans, qui terminera le 31 décembre son deuxième mandat de cinq ans comme chef de l'ONU. Jusqu'à présent, la Costaricaine Rebeca Grynspan, 70 ans, qui dirigeait l'agence de l'ONU pour le Commerce et le Développement (Cnuced), faisait la course en tête. Lors du vote de vendredi, tenu à huis clos, les quinze membres du Conseil de sécurité ont anonymement assigné à chaque candidat une mention : « encourage », « décourage » ou « sans opinion ». Mais pour la première fois, le vote des cinq membres permanents apparaissait en couleur. Avec neuf « encourage », Rebeca Grynspan arrive encore en tête du vote, mais elle a également reçu cinq « décourage », dont deux émanant de membres permanents, et un « sans opinion ». Derrière elle arrive l'actuel dirigeant de l'Agence internationale de l'énergie atomique (AIEA), l'Argentin Rafael Grossi, 65 ans, avec huit « encourage », six « décourage », dont deux membres permanents, et un « sans opinion ». Ce processus intervient alors que l'ONU traverse l'une des périodes les plus difficiles de son histoire, confrontée à une multiplication des conflits, à des divisions persistantes au Conseil de sécurité et à de graves difficultés financières. AFP

items.title: Gunmen kill two at Plateau mining site
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed two persons at a mining site in Burdinga, Gashish District of Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM) has confirmed. The victims, identified as Goodluck Bulus and Emmanuel Monday, both in their mid-20s, were reportedly killed on Friday, in an attack that has renewed concerns over persistent insecurity in the area. Our correspondent gathered that the gunmen stormed the mining site at about 6pm and opened fire on the miners, killing the two young men. The National Publicity Secretary of BYM, Rwang Tengwong, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, condemned the killings and called on the Plateau State Government and security agencies to take urgent action. In a statement, Tengwong said, “The Berom Youth Moulders Association, under the leadership of its National President, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, strongly condemns the killing of two young men at a mining site in Burdinga, Gashish District, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.” He said, “The victims, identified as Goodluck Bulus and Emmanuel Monday, both in their mid-20s, represent yet another painful loss of young lives in a community already burdened by years of insecurity.” The BYM spokesman said the killing was particularly heartbreaking because Goodluck’s father was reportedly killed in an attack more than a decade ago. “More heartbreaking is the report that Goodluck’s father was killed in an attack by Fulani herdsmen more than a decade ago,” he said. The association described the killings in the state by gunmen as a painful reminder of the human cost of insecurity, saying the incidents had left families devastated and communities living in fear. “These are not mere statistics; they are human lives cut short, families shattered, and communities left in fear,” Tengwong said. He called on the Plateau State Government and relevant security agencies to investigate the killings and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted. “We therefore call on the Plateau State Government and relevant security agencies to urgently investigate these killings, apprehend and prosecute the perpetrators, strengthen security surveillance around mining sites and vulnerable communities, and establish effective measures to protect residents and commuters,” he said. The BYM spokesman also called for sustained security operations and intelligence-driven interventions to prevent further attacks, abductions and killings across the state. “We also demand sustained security operations and intelligence-driven interventions to prevent further attacks, abductions and killings across Plateau State,” he said. He added, “The continued loss of innocent lives must not become normalised. The people deserve protection, the victims deserve justice, and the perpetrators must be held accountable.” The post Gunmen kill two at Plateau mining site appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Guinée : Les réserves foncières de Simbayah Wanindara et de Kassa déclassées (décret)
items.description: Dans un décret lu ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026, le président de la République a prononcé le déclassement des réserves foncières de la zone industrielle de Simbayah Wanindara, à Conakry, et de l’île de Kassa. La décision prévoit la restructuration, la régularisation et l’aménagement de ces sites au profit de leurs occupants. Selon le décret, la réserve foncière de Simbayah Wanindara, objet du titre foncier numéro 23-190-2018-TF de Conakry, couvre une superficie de 315 hectares, 38 ares et 35 centiares. Elle avait été visée par le décret numéro 211-PRG-SGG-89 du 23 novembre 1989. La réserve foncière de l’île de Kassa, enregistrée sous le titre foncier numéro 23-267-2018-TF de Conakry, est également concernée par cette mesure. L’article 2 du décret précise que ces deux sites feront l’objet d’opérations de restructuration, de régularisation et d’aménagement conformément aux dispositions du Code de l’urbanisme et du Code foncier et domanial. Toutefois, certaines parcelles et installations sont exclues de cette décision. Il s’agit notamment des terrains ayant fait l’objet de baux emphytéotiques ou de baux à construction, des équipements publics, dont les écoles, les centres de santé, les terrains de sport, les espaces verts et les cimetières. Les lieux de culte, les installations des forces de défense et de sécurité, les servitudes ainsi que les emprises de la route Leprince, des transversales et des routes secondaires sont également exclus du champ d’application du décret. Les ministres chargés de l’Urbanisme et de l’Aménagement du territoire, de la Défense nationale, de l’Administration du territoire et de la Sécurité sont chargés de l’application de cette décision, chacun en ce qui le concerne.

items.title: CompuGhana launches cashback festival with two BYD cars, cash prizes on offer
items.description: Technology retailer CompuGhana has launched a cashback sales festival, offering customers the opportunity to win two brand-new 2026 BYD vehicles, cash prizes, and other electronic appliances. The campaign, which runs from October 19 through December 2026, will reward customers who make purchases of at least GH¢1,000 with the chance to enter a promotional raffle draw. Marketing Manager at CompuGhana Limited, Rita Akua Safowaa Nyarko, said the initiative goes beyond a sales promotion and forms part of the company’s commitment to rewarding customers. She described the festival as an opportunity to combine technology, value and customer rewards to create what the company calls the ultimate shopping experience. “Cashback Sales Festival is more than a sales promotion. It is our way of bringing together great value, technology, rewards and customer experiences to create what we proudly call the Cashback Sales Festival, the ultimate shopping experience,” she said. Customers who spend at least GH¢1,000 at CompuGhana showrooms can enter the raffle by scanning a QR code available at the outlets or accessing it later on the company’s website. The first draw is scheduled for November 20, when one of the cars and other prizes will be awarded. A second draw in December will offer the remaining car and additional prizes. Brand ambassador for CompuGhana, Tima Kumkum, has cautioned customers to be vigilant against fraudsters seeking to exploit the promotion. She urged the public to engage only with the company’s verified social media accounts, warning that several fake accounts operate under similar names. General Manager of CompuGhana, Haissam Kassar, expressed appreciation to existing customers for their loyalty, noting that their support had contributed to the company’s growth and development. “Without our customers, we’ve not been learning, improving and evolving to where we are now,” he said. He added that the company had spent several months preparing for the campaign and was looking forward to bringing the festival experience to its showrooms. The cashback sales festival is expected to run through December 2026, with the promotional draws certified by the National Lottery Authority.

items.title: UFOA-A U20 : Grâce à Moussa Gueye, le Sénégal bat la Mauritanie
items.description: Le Sénégal est bien entré dans son tournoi. Mené dès le premier quart d'heure, les Lionceaux des moins de 20 ans ont battu la Mauritanie (2-1) ce vendredi au stade Mamadou-Konaté de Bamako, pour leur match d'ouverture du tournoi UFOA-A. Les Mauritaniens ont frappé les premiers. À la 13e minute, Imam Dine Sow (Nouakchott Academy) a profité d'une sortie hasardeuse du gardien sénégalais Baye Galaye Dieng pour glisser le ballon dans le but vide. Néanmoins, les hommes de Malick Daf n'ont pas tardé à répondre. Avant la pause, Moussa Gueye a rétabli l'équilibre d'une frappe puissante, imparable pour le portier mauritanien Brahim Hemedy. Les deux équipes ont regagné les vestiaires à égalité (1-1). Évoluant à Mérida AD, Gueye est le seul joueur évoluant à l'étranger parmi les 25 retenus par le sélectionneur. Une tête décisive à la 84e En seconde période, les Sénégalais ont continué de pousser. Leur insistance a payé à la 84e minute : Moussa Gueye s'est élevé pour placer une tête et battre à nouveau Brahim Hemedy, offrant la victoire à son équipe. Cette victoire place le Sénégal en bonne position dans le groupe B, qui comprend aussi la Sierra Leone et la Guinée-Bissau. Mais cette dernière a déclaré forfait, selon l'UFOA, quelques heures avant le coup d'envoi du match des Lionceaux. Le Sénégal, qui devait l'affronter lors de la deuxième journée, restera donc au repos. Il reprendra la compétition le 22 octobre à 16 h, face à la Sierra Leone, dans le même stade Mamadou-Konaté, pour la troisième journée de la phase de groupes. O.B.N

items.title: Church of Pentecost warns teachers against sexual abuse and harassment of female students
items.description: The Church of Pentecost’s Schools Outreach Ministry has warned teachers against sexually abusing, harassing or bullying female students, urging educators to uphold professional ethics and protect children in their care. The warning comes amid findings by the JoyNews Research Team, which has tracked at least 44 cases of sexual abuse involving teachers since 2015. School heads accounted for 40 per cent of recent cases identified by the team. Speaking at an event organised in collaboration with the Ghana Education Service (GES) to mark the International Day of the Girl Child, the ministry’s chairman, Rev. Joseph Buertey, condemned the conduct and said it contradicted the fundamental responsibilities of teachers. “If you are a teacher and you are abusing a girl, harassing a girl, you are sleeping with a girl, what it means is that you don’t understand your profession,” he said. Rev. Buertey said teachers were expected to educate, empower and prepare students for the future, not exploit them for personal gain. “You are there to teach these girls, you are there to empower them, you are there to build a future. You are not there to exploit them,” he stated. He warned that teachers found engaging in such misconduct would face legal consequences. “When you are discovered, the law will deal with you,” he cautioned. The event also highlighted the need to involve boys in discussions about girls’ education, safety and protection. Korle Klottey Municipal Education Director Ebenezer Perry Ofori said efforts to empower girls should be accompanied by initiatives to guide boys and help them understand the challenges their female counterparts face. He questioned whether enough attention was being paid to boys as programmes to support girls continued. “As we concentrate so much on the girls, we realise that the girls will be shining and shining and shining. What is happening to the boys?” he asked. Mr Ofori said raising boys and girls together would promote balance and mutual understanding. “We need to also ensure that we bring the boys up; we have to bring them along so that together we get the two of them on the same scale for a balance,” he said. A student who attended the event, Celestine Kporfor, said the discussions had reinforced her belief in the importance of educating girls. She urged parents and guardians to invest in their daughters’ education, describing it as an important contribution to their future and national development. “When you educate your daughter, you have made the best decision in this world,” she said. The event brought together students from basic and senior high schools across the Korle Klottey Municipality to promote girls’ education, raise awareness about their protection, and encourage stakeholders to make schools safer. The engagement forms part of broader efforts to protect the rights of girls and ensure that schools remain safe environments for learning and personal development.

items.title: Enugu Corps member’s death not caused by substandard medicines – NAFDAC
items.description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has debunked reports that a Corp member whose death occurred in Enugu died of effects of substandard and falsified medicines. This is contained in a statement by the Director-General of the agency, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye, in Abuja on Friday. The statement noted that the deceased Corp member previously at NYSC Orientation Camp, Awgu, in Enugu State, did not die of what people insinuated. According to the statement, preliminary investigations revealed that the Corp member was brought to the Camp clinic aided by two other Corp members on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at about 9:00pm with symptoms suggestive of severe malaria and a known peptic ulcer disease patient. The statement stated that the deceased was however, stabilised with intramuscular antimalarial and other supportive medications given intravenously. It stated that the deceased was placed on bed rest for observation till Oct 8 morning when he was discharged with oral medications. “He came back unaided on Saturday, Oct. 10, with complaints of right thigh pain for which he was asked to see a physiotherapist. “His profuse sweating caught the attention of the medical doctor, who measured his blood pressure and found it to be low (80/40 mmHg). He was stabilised with intravenous Normal Saline. “Serial monitoring showed recurrent episodes of hypertension. This development, coupled with poor urine output despite adequate fluid resuscitations, prompted his referral to the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu State, in an ambulance accompanied by another doctor. “He went into a coma at about the time of arriving at the UNTH. All efforts at resuscitating him failed. “His friend later informed the Camp clinic doctor that his deceased friend was vomiting for two days after the initial admission at the camp. The doctor was not aware of this development. “It is instructive to note that the same medications given to the deceased were also administered to several other patients in the camp who got well after receiving their treatments. “The medical doctors, pharmacists, and other healthcare workers at the camp clinic not only prescribed but also used the medications by themselves at different times,” the statement said. According to the statement, the doctors believed that the cause of death was acute kidney injury secondary to severe dehydration and shock in the meantime. It stated that NAFDAC officers had visited the clinic, interviewed the doctors and other staff and taken samples of the medications for further necessary actions which included laboratory analysis. The NAFDAC commiserates with the family of the late Youth Corp member and prays that God grants the family the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. NAFDAC, however, enjoined the general public to remain calm as the agency was taking all necessary steps to ensure that all medicines made available to the public were safe and of good quality and efficacious. It advised the public to call the NAFDAC Call Centre on the following lines: 0800-1-623322 or 0700-1-623322 for complaints and enquiries. The agency also advised the general public to email reforms@nafdac.gov.ng (NAN). The post Enugu Corps member’s death not caused by substandard medicines – NAFDAC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sud SARL : Abdoulaye Boubou Thiam et Cheikh Ahmeth Touré désignés cogérants
items.description: Le groupe Sud Communication ouvre un nouveau chapitre. L'Assemblée générale extraordinaire de Sud SARL a désigné Abdoulaye Boubou Thiam et Cheikh Ahmeth Touré cogérants de la société, après le décès de son gérant statutaire, Babacar Touré. La section Synpics de Sud Communication l'a fait savoir dans un communiqué. Réunie le 10 septembre 2026 dans les locaux de Sud Quotidien, l'assemblée était présidée par Me Sonko, mandataire judiciaire délégué. Les associés ont adopté les résolutions portant sur « la constatation du décès de Babacar Touré, gérant statutaire de la société », ainsi que sur la désignation des deux nouveaux responsables. Ils ont aussi approuvé une modification de l'article 12 des statuts, « afin de tenir compte de la nouvelle configuration de la gérance ». Sud SARL est la société éditrice de Sud Quotidien et l'actionnaire majoritaire de Sen Radio, qui diffuse Sud FM. Restructurer et préserver l'héritage Pour le syndicat, l'enjeu est désormais double. Il s'agit de « restructurer la société » tout en préservant « l'héritage professionnel et éditorial de Babacar Touré et de ses camarades, pères fondateurs du groupe ». La section Synpics adresse ses « chaleureuses félicitations » aux deux cogérants. Elle affirme sa « détermination à travailler avec les nouveaux cogérants » pour relever ensemble le défi de la restructuration, conformément à la feuille de route fixée par l'Assemblée générale des associés. Le communiqué adresse aussi des remerciements. Le syndicat exprime sa « profonde gratitude » à Vieux Savané et à Ndiaga Sylla, pour les sacrifices consentis ces dernières années afin de maintenir Sud SARL à flot, « dans un environnement économique national particulièrement difficile ». Il remercie enfin la famille de feu Babacar Touré ainsi que les anciens de Sud Quotidien, dont il salue le « soutien » et l' « engagement sans faille » pour la sauvegarde du groupe, qu'il qualifie de « véritable patrimoine national des médias au Sénégal ». items.title: GAPTE intensifies efforts to increase bus availability for Aayalolo contra-flow system
items.description: The Greater Accra Passenger Transport Executive (GAPTE) has intensified efforts to increase the number of buses available for its Aayalolo contra-flow service. The effort is to enable the company to meet growing passenger demand and support plans to extend the initiative to more corridors in the Greater Accra Region. The Managing Director of GAPTE, Dawuda Awudu, who disclosed this in an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) on Thursday, said the organisation was repairing broken-down buses and engaging the sector minister to explore the possibility of acquiring additional vehicles to strengthen operations. “We are trying as much as possible to repair, and the repairs are still going on at the depot. We would be able to add to ease the pressure,” he said. The contra-flow system was introduced on September 29, 2026, to ease passenger congestion in Accra during peak hours of the day. Currently, it operates on three major corridors, namely: Accra-Adenta, Accra-Kasoa and Accra-Amasaman. Mr Awudu said the system had significantly reduced commuting times and improved mobility since its introduction some two weeks ago. He indicated that the initiative had attracted considerable patronage because of its efficiency and reliability, creating pressure on the available fleet, particularly during peak hours. He said the organisation was assessing the performance of the existing corridors before extending the service to other routes, with safety and adequate bus availability remaining key considerations. Mr Awudu said commuters travelling from Adenta to Accra’s Central Business District (CBD), who previously spent about two hours in traffic, could now complete the journey in an average of 28 minutes during the morning peak period. Similarly, travel time from Amasaman to the CBD had reduced from more than three hours to about 35 minutes, while the Kasoa corridor recorded an average journey time of approximately 50 minutes. He said the improvements were benefiting workers, traders and students while helping to reduce congestion on major roads. Mr Awudu explained that the primary objective of the service was to improve public mobility rather than maximise revenue, describing the initiative as a social intervention aimed at making transportation more accessible and affordable. “Our profit is translated into easing congestion in Greater Accra and enhancing mobility,” he said. On compliance, he said public education and sensitisation had improved motorists’ understanding of the system, while buses operated in convoys led by motorcyclists to enhance safety and alert oncoming traffic. He urged commercial transport operators, private motorists and other stakeholders to support the initiative, stressing that cooperation was essential to sustaining its benefits. “Our focus has always been to ease congestion,” he said. Mr Awudu assured the public of GAPTE’s commitment to improving service reliability and expanding the system when operational capacity permitted.

items.title: Five Fabulous Days of Katie Zacharia
items.description: The world will little note, nor long remember, the Katie Zacharia era. Indeed, the tenure of the second White House press secretary of Donald Trump’s second term, which ended after five days and a single, 14-minute press conference, is already receding into memory. Yet what matters more than her press-secretarial contributions, or the ideas she stood for, is the period Zacharia represents: the Trump administration’s reversion to the hapless chaos of the president’s first term. Trump’s initial go-round was primarily a farce, setting bumbling aides against challenges such as finding the light switches in the Cabinet room, hurling burgers against the White House wall, and booking the wrong Four Seasons. Trump cycled through personnel like Spinal Tap drummers, as one hired helper after the next left in frustration or shame. The second term has operated with, if not normality, at least comparative efficiency. Chief of Staff Susie Wiles turned the executive branch from an exploding fireworks factory into a machine relentlessly processing the president’s whims into law. [ Read: Trump’s secret points system for Cabinet members ] Yet as the midterm elections draw near, the machine has begun to sputter. In the span of days, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced he would livestream a public execution, only for Trump to overrule him; the administration fired Kimberly Guilfoyle, its ambassador to Greece, for engaging in corruption so overt, it embarrassed even the most corrupt administration in history; and Politico reported that Trump is asking his friends what they think of Wiles, which is historically the prelude to his turning on an underling. In the midst of this multicar pileup, Zacharia briefly stepped forward as the administration’s stammering face. If you have ever felt awkward in a public setting, her single press conference was the stuff of recurrent nightmares. Zacharia read from the podium, head down, in the tone of a third-grade book report delivered verbally in front of the entire school by a child with crippling anxiety. She had to pause multiple times to take gulps of air. Trump, she said in one typical segment, “had a historic one-day war, and now we are, have a booming economy, and a great relationship”—here she stopped to catch herself—“with Venezuela. The U.S. achieved record domestic oil and gas production in 2025 and record crude and petroleum product exports in 2026.” At another point, attempting to discuss nuclear-power plants, she called them “something President Trump is delivering on, just like he delivers on every promise.” (Pause, gasp for breath.) “In addition to that, it, we will be, it, we will be, there is $54 billion tied to the Alaska LNG pipeline.” Then she told the assembled reporters, “My goal is to be able to communicate that in complete tandem with the president, as he is his own best spokesperson, and will absolutely be leading the way as—with that.” It was as if the notion that Trump could do her job much better than she could had intruded into her thoughts and made its way out of her mouth. She wrapped up the press conference after answering only three questions. [ Tom Nichols: Kimberly Guilfoyle broke Trump’s most important rule ] Shortly after, she appeared with the president on the White House lawn, and when a reporter asked which state’s bar exam she had passed—Zacharia has described herself as an attorney—she replied, mysteriously, “When I moved to China.” Matters fell apart quickly. She appeared on Sean Hannity’s show, perhaps expecting the tender treatment for which Hannity is so synonymous that his last name has become a portmanteau, hannitize , for friendly damage control. Instead he subjected her to an interrogation for which she was predictably unprepared. Indeed, her defense consisted of describing herself as unprepared. “What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate with very little prep time. Given the fact that I’d been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day.” Sometimes, your best just isn’t good enough. So it was with Zacharia. So it is with the whole administration—mired in a losing war and persistent inflation, and flailing about for people to blame for the debacle. People who aren’t Donald Trump.

items.title: Aayalolo contra-flow moves over 8,000 passengers daily – GAPTE boss
items.description: More than 8,000 passengers are transported daily by the Aayalolo contra-flow system being implemented by the government to ease passenger congestion in Accra at peak hours. The system, which was introduced on September 29, 2026, currently operates on three major corridors of Adenta, Amasaman and Kasoa. The Managing Director of GAPTE, Dawuda Awudu, in an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) on Thursday, said the initiative had improved mobility and helped commuters save considerable time on their daily journeys. He said each Aayalolo bus could accommodate about 85 passengers, enabling the service to transport thousands of commuters through multiple trips daily. “Look at one Aayalolo bus that takes around 85 passengers. If you have 10 of the buses, you are talking about 850 passengers per trip,” he said. He explained that with 10 buses making multiple trips, the system could move more than 8,000 passengers, helping to reduce pressure on the roads and improve access to public transport. Mr Awudu also acknowledged improvement in travel time under the contra-flow. He noted that commuters travelling from Adenta to the Central Business District (CBD), who previously spent about two hours on the journey, could now complete it in an average of 28 minutes during the morning peak period. In the evening, the journey from the CBD to Adenta took approximately 30 minutes, compared with the usual two-and-a-half hours. He said travel time from Amasaman to Accra had also dropped from more than three hours to about 35 minutes in the morning and an average of 40 minutes in the evening. On the Kasoa corridor, commuters could complete their journeys in approximately 50 minutes, representing a substantial reduction in travel time. The MD said the improvements had benefited workers, traders and students, while encouraging private vehicle owners to use the system to reduce congestion on the roads. Mr Awudu also noted that public compliance had improved following extensive education and sensitisation campaigns, supported by text messages and media advertisements. He said escorts of these buses by the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Police Service had improved safety and alerted motorists approaching the contra-flow lanes. GAPTE, he said, was assessing the initial results before extending the system to other established corridors. He said the expansion would depend on safety considerations and the availability of additional buses, with repairs ongoing and discussions underway with the sector minister to strengthen the fleet. He also dismissed calls about the profitability of the initiative, explaining that the system was more of a social intervention than a profit-oriented one. “Our profit is translated into easing congestion in Greater Accra and enhancing mobility,” he said. Mr Awudu urged commercial transport operators, private motorists and other stakeholders to support the initiative, stressing that its primary objective was to reduce congestion rather than displace trotro operators. He assured that GAPTE would continue to collaborate with relevant transport and road safety authorities to improve the service and make public transport more reliable.

items.title: DSS, military, police arrest 5 over NYSC members kidnap
items.description: …As 3 others escape with gunshot injuries By Soni Daniel Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), the military and police have arrested five suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly responsible for the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Imo State on Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day. Five other suspected members of the gang, however, escaped with gunshot injuries prompting a massive manhunt for them. The suspects were apprehended during a series of intelligence-led operations conducted at different locations in Rivers and Abia States. However, in the course of the operation, three other suspects escaped with varying degrees of injury. Security sources disclosed that the operations were carried out between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State and Aba South LGA. Abia State. Recall that 20 NYSC members were abducted by armed men along Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, as they travelled to their assigned orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The victims were subsequently rescued on October 7, 2026, during a joint security operation at Amakohia Ubi Village. The string of operations mark a significant breakthrough in efforts to track down the perpetrators, dismantle the criminal network allegedly responsible for the abduction and bring those involved to justice. A security source described the development as a major relief, noting that security agencies had sustained a wide-ranging manhunt for the abductors. “This is a huge sigh of relief. Security agencies have been on a manhunt for the abductors, and we are elated that they have been captured. We strongly believe they will be charged to Court by DSS and the corps members will get justice,” the source said. items.title: NSIB probes private jet after door falls mid-air
items.description: A private jet operated by Triton Aviation made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after losing a door mid-air on Thursday. The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) confirmed the incident to TheCable on Friday, saying an investigation had commenced. “The incident happened yesterday and investigations are ongoing,” a source at the bureau said. According to a report by Punch on Friday, the aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was heading to the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred at about 4:20 pm. Citing an incident report, the publication said the aircraft was about three nautical miles from the airport and climbing through 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call. “Mayday, Mayday, Mayday,” the crew reportedly transmitted. Following the distress call, airport fire and emergency personnel, alongside the medical team, were alerted and placed on standby. Fire and rescue teams were also directed to designated positions in preparation for the aircraft’s return. The report further stated that at about 4:29 pm UTC, while communicating with the Abuja control tower, the crew asked whether air traffic controllers could confirm if the door was open. “The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft using binoculars, but could not establish the door’s condition because of the aircraft’s position. The crew was subsequently informed that the controller could not confirm the situation visually,” the report said. The aircraft subsequently landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 pm UTC, about 14 minutes after the Mayday call. Following the landing, the duty controller reportedly observed that the aircraft’s door was missing from the fuselage. The jet was then taxied to the international apron extension and parked with the assistance of a marshaller. Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media showed what appeared to be an aircraft door lying on farmland near Abuja. According to Billionaires.Africa, the NSIB confirmed that the door had been recovered. “The door has been recovered and secured at the NSIB wreckage hangar,” the bureau said. The NSIB said it had commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and would provide updates as the investigation progresses. items.title: 2027: Adebutu’s omission from INEC list unintentional — Sowunmi-Kolapo
items.description: …Says omission will be addressed soon, insists PDP candidate will win By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Deputy Governorship Candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2027 Ogun State governorship election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has expressed confidence that the omission of her principal, Ladi Adebutu, from a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) was unintentional and would be addressed soon. Sowunmi-Kolapo also expressed confidence that Adebutu would emerge as the next governor of Ogun State in the 2027 election, describing recent political developments in the state as signs of the ticket’s growing prospects. She spoke with journalists and Muslim faithful shortly after Jumat prayers at the headquarters of the Nawair-ud-Deen Society in Abeokuta on Friday. The gathering featured prayers for the PDP governorship ticket, with leaders of the Muslim society expressing support for Sowunmi-Kolapo and Adebutu ahead of the election. The Chief Imam of the Nawair-ud-Deen Society’s Abeokuta headquarters and Ogun State, Sheikh Tiamiyu Olamigoke, led other Islamic leaders in prayers for the candidates’ success and the continued peace and development of Ogun State. The clerics acknowledged Sowunmi-Kolapo’s contributions to the Muslim community and her record of service before venturing into partisan politics, expressing confidence that she would demonstrate compassion and commitment to public service if elected alongside Adebutu. They also cited Adebutu’s contributions to the development of Ogun State, including his support for the Muslim community, as reasons he deserved the electorate’s backing. Addressing the controversy surrounding the INEC list, Sowunmi-Kolapo dismissed suggestions that Adebutu’s omission, alongside celebrations reportedly witnessed among members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), indicated an advantage for the party ahead of the 2027 governorship election. She maintained that the omission was not deliberate and would be resolved by the electoral commission. Sowunmi-Kolapo described the appointment of Professor Joash Amupitan as INEC chairman as one of the appointments she believed President Bola Tinubu had got right. She described Amupitan as a globally recognised professional and expressed confidence that he would protect his reputation by upholding the integrity of the electoral process. While acknowledging the pressures associated with the position, the PDP deputy governorship candidate said she remained optimistic that the INEC chairman would discharge his responsibilities professionally. She also expressed confidence in Tinubu’s commitment to ensuring free, fair and credible elections, irrespective of the political interests involved. Reacting to the excitement reportedly expressed by APC members following the publication of the INEC list, Sowunmi-Kolapo described their reaction as premature, insisting that it would not determine the outcome of the 2027 governorship election. “They are ‘soon-to-be IDPs (Internally Displaced Politicians),’ exhibiting the symptoms of ‘IDPA (Impending Defeat Panic Attack),’” she said with laughter. She maintained that no force could stop what she described as a genuine movement driven by people determined to protect their heritage and secure a better future for coming generations. “We will soon separate the wheat from the chaff. There is a difference between those fighting for their pockets or struggling to retain their juicy positions and those fighting to protect our heritage in the interest of generations of genuine Ogun indigenes, who must not be relegated to second-class citizens by imported leaders,” she said. Sowunmi-Kolapo stressed the need for Ogun State’s resources to be deployed for the benefit of its people, describing the principle as the foundation of the PDP’s ITURA DE agenda. “Ogun’s resources must work for its people. This is the bedrock of our ITURA DE mandate. A PDP administration led by Hon. Ladi Adebutu will prioritise the welfare of citizens and ensure real financial autonomy for local governments, with a view to promoting accountability and effective service delivery at the grassroots,” she said. Earlier, the Otun Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Iya Sunnah of the Nawair-ud-Deen Society, Alhaja Risikat Ogunfemi, urged members of the society, the Egba Muslim Community and the wider Ogun State Muslim Community to support Sowunmi-Kolapo and Adebutu. Ogunfemi described the deputy governorship candidate as a source of pride to the Muslim community and expressed confidence that she would prioritise the welfare of the people if elected alongside Adebutu. The gathering ended with prayers by imams and Islamic scholars for the protection and success of the PDP candidates in the 2027 election, as well as peace, progress and prosperity in Ogun State. The post 2027: Adebutu’s omission from INEC list unintentional — Sowunmi-Kolapo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Place à la joie, s’il vous plaît! (Par Cheikh Mamoudou Niang)
items.description: Organiser un événement mondial comme les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ), consacré à la jeunesse du monde, est une occasion historique. C’est aussi un immense défi pour un pays et pour tout un peuple, particulièrement à un moment où, dans plusieurs sociétés, les jeunes expriment leur colère, leurs inquiétudes et leurs aspirations. Premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse organisés en Afrique, les JOJ de Dakar placent le Sénégal sous le regard du monde. Au-delà de la compétition sportive, notre pays a l’occasion de montrer une Afrique ambitieuse, accueillante et pleinement actrice de son avenir. Cette occasion prend un relief particulier dans un contexte où les préjugés sur le continent persistent et où des sportifs africains sont encore victimes d’insultes racistes dans certains stades européens. Le Sénégal joue donc bien davantage qu’une organisation logistique : il engage une part de son image, de sa diplomatie et de sa capacité à inspirer confiance. À l’heure où son avenir économique et financier exige des choix difficiles, cet événement peut devenir un puissant levier de « soft power », à condition d’en faire une fête réussie, ouverte et fédératrice. Or, à l’approche de l’ouverture, le climat politico-social ne semble pas encore à la hauteur de l’enthousiasme que nous souhaiterions offrir à nos futurs hôtes. Les difficultés économiques et sociales pèsent sur les ménages, tandis que les tensions politico-sociales occupent l’espace public. Certains syndicats appellent à la grève ces jours. Celui de la RTS menace même de boycotter la retransmission des JOJ. Inacceptable en épée de Damoclès chantage pour leur Pays. La joie, elle, ne se décrète pas : elle se construit par la confiance, le respect et le sentiment de partager un destin commun. Une scène de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations 2023 en Côte d’Ivoire m’est revenue en mémoire. Après la lourde défaite des Éléphants face à la Guinée équatoriale, lors de la phase de groupes, un gérant de bar et de restaurant, amer et inquiet, avait résumé son état d’esprit par ces mots : « Nous voulons la joie, rien que la joie. » Il ne savait pas encore que son pays allait finalement remporter la compétition, dans un retournement devenu une immense source de bonheur collectif. Cette phrase me parle aujourd’hui. Nous voulons, nous aussi, retrouver la joie dans notre pays : la joie dans nos cœurs, dans nos relations humaines et dans notre capacité à nous parler malgré nos désaccords. Une nation ne se résume ni à ses crises ni à ses querelles politiques. Elle se mesure aussi à sa faculté de se rassembler lorsque l’occasion l’exige. C’est dans cet esprit que le calendrier des auditions annoncées par une commission parlementaire sur la gestion des fonds publics de 2012 à 2026 mérite, à mes yeux, d’être interrogé. La reddition des comptes est une exigence démocratique fondamentale. Elle doit se poursuivre dans le respect des règles et de la vérité. Mais était-il opportun d’ouvrir cette séquence à l’approche des JOJ, alors que le pays s’apprête à accueillir la jeunesse du monde et que le vote du budget 2027 constitue également une échéance majeure ? Un autre calendrier aurait peut-être permis de préserver davantage l’attention collective, sans renoncer à la transparence ni à la justice. Il ne s’agit pas de demander au pays de détourner le regard de ses difficultés, encore moins de suspendre le débat démocratique. Il s’agit de rappeler que la responsabilité politique consiste aussi à mesurer les moments, les priorités et les conséquences de ses décisions. La vérité et la justice sont indispensables à la réconciliation nationale ; la lucidité et le sens du moment le sont tout autant. Ne laissons pas les tensions éteindre notre capacité à espérer et à sourire. La joie partagée peut devenir l’un des premiers pas vers une confiance retrouvée. Elle est une énergie collective : celle d’un peuple déterminé à vivre ensemble, à accueillir dignement ses invités et à offrir à sa jeunesse des raisons de croire en l’avenir. Sourions entre nous et ouvrons nos bras à la jeunesse du monde qui arrive au pays de la Téranga. Nous lui avons promis l’hospitalité ; faisons-en une expérience vivante, sincère et mémorable. Ayoo — ou, comme le diraient nos frères et sœurs halpulaar, Haayo : bienvenue dans la joie, au Sénégal, pays de la Téranga. Cheikh Mamoudou Niang Citoyen sénégalais et patriote Sénégal Rek ! Un Peuple – Un But – Une Foi

items.title: Des élèves-stagiaires sénégalais de retour partagent leurs expériences
items.description: La résidence de l’ambassadeur du Japon au Sénégal sise à Dakar Fann, a abrité le mercredi dernier une cérémonie de restitution de 24 élèves stagiaires sénégalais rentrés du Japon où ils ont séjourné du 23 août au 3 septembre derniers dans le programme Japon-Afrique pour la jeunesse (Japan-Africa Youth Programme). Douze élèves du lycée Thierno Saïdou Nourou Tall et douze autres du Centre de formation professionnelle et technique (Cfpt) Sénégal/Japon ont séjourné du 23 août au 3 septembre 2026 au Japon dans le Programme Japon-Afrique pour la jeunesse (Japan-Africa Youth Program). Une initiative d'échanges internationaux lancée par le gouvernement du Japon à la suite de la 9e Conférence internationale de Tokyo sur le développement de l'Afrique (Ticad 9). De retour au Sénégal, ceux-ci ont expliqué leurs expériences au pays du soleil levant. Ouvrant la cérémonie, l'ambassadeur du Japon au Sénégal, Takeshi Akamatsu, est longuement revenu sur les liens de fraternité qui unissent les deux pays. « Ces relations sont symbolisées par une école à Dakar dénommée Sénégal/Japon », a-t-il rappelé, soulignant que la visite de ces élèves vise à faire découvrir davantage aux jeunes africains la culture nippone et les avancées technologiques du pays. S'adressant directement aux bénéficiaires, le diplomate les a invités « à devenir chacun à sa manière, des jeunes capables de créer des liens entre le Sénégal et le Japon ». Il les a également exhortés à partager et à raconter leur voyage à leurs amis et à poursuivre l'apprentissage de la langue japonaise. Il a évoqué aussi la question de la disponibilité de bourses d'études pour ceux qui souhaitent poursuivre leur cursus dans les universités japonaises. Ibrahima Maïga, un des bénéficiaires de l’initiative, a fait savoir que le programme va se poursuivre à travers la construction d'un plan d'action durable baptisé « Be the voice (être la voix) ». Un dispositif qui consiste à partager leurs expériences avec des élèves du Cfpt Sénégal/Japon, à travers des présentations et des vidéos diffusées sur le site de l'établissement. Élève en 2e année de Brevet de technicien supérieur (Bts) en Informatique, industrie et réseaux, M. Maïga a également indiqué qu'au cours de leur séjour, qu’ils ont visité différents endroits, notamment l'Université d'Ashikaga, des laboratoires et le National Institute of Technology, plus connu sous le nom d'Oyama Kosen. Il s'est dit « touché » par la discipline des étudiants japonais, la qualité du travail en groupe et l'usage d'équipements de pointe dans les laboratoires. Prenant la parole, Bacary Badji, directeur des études du Cfpt Sénégal/Japon, a salué le long compagnonnage entre les deux pays. Il a toutefois rappelé que ces liens doivent être entretenus et renforcés pour accompagner davantage ce centre fondé en 1984 grâce à la coopération bilatérale, soulignant que ce retour au bercail de ces élèves marque le début d'une nouvelle mission. Aziz Méthiour NDIAYE (Stagiaire)

items.title: Ghana to host UN convention signing on digital cargo documents on October 26
items.description: Ghana is set to host the signing ceremony for the United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents on October 26, 2026, in a move expected to support the digitalisation of trade documentation and improve the efficiency of cross-border transactions. Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA), Professor Ransford Gyampo, says the Convention will establish a harmonised legal framework for electronic negotiable cargo documents, helping address delays, administrative costs and fraud risks associated with paper-based trade documentation. Speaking at a media engagement in Accra on October 15, 2026, ahead of the signing ceremony, Professor Gyampo said the initiative would provide the legal foundation for electronic documents to perform the functions of their paper-based equivalents, subject to the Convention’s requirements. “The continued dependence on paper documents can create delays, increase administrative costs, expose transactions to fraud and complicate the movement of goods across borders,” he said. Negotiable cargo documents, including bills of lading, play an important role in international commerce by facilitating cargo movement, supporting commercial transactions and providing a basis for trade finance. The Convention is expected to create opportunities to reduce documentation-related delays, improve transaction efficiency and facilitate access to trade finance, while supporting more integrated digital supply chains. Professor Gyampo stressed that the initiative goes beyond replacing paper documents with electronic records, arguing that legal certainty and confidence are essential to the digital transformation of international trade. “The Convention is therefore not simply about replacing paper with electronic records. It is about building the legal certainty and confidence necessary for businesses and institutions to conduct trade in an increasingly digital environment,” he said. For Ghana, hosting the signing ceremony presents an opportunity to demonstrate its commitment to trade facilitation, digital transformation and stronger regional and international trade connectivity. Professor Gyampo said the development also aligns with Ghana’s ambition to strengthen its position as a preferred trade and logistics hub in West Africa and advance the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The Convention is considered particularly relevant to African trade, where cross-border transactions often involve multiple jurisdictions, transport modes and border procedures. According to Professor Gyampo, a reliable legal framework for electronic negotiable cargo documents could help reduce documentary barriers, improve the flow of trade-related information and support more efficient cargo movement across supply chains. For Ghanaian importers and exporters, the expected benefits include lower administrative burdens, faster processing of trade transactions, improved opportunities for trade financing and greater predictability in international commerce. However, Professor Gyampo cautioned that the benefits would depend on sustained efforts beyond the signing ceremony, including the Convention’s adoption, ratification and implementation, as well as the preparedness of businesses, financial institutions, transport operators and regulators to use electronic negotiable cargo documents. “These benefits will not arise from the signing ceremony alone,” he said, calling for continued stakeholder engagement and the necessary legal, institutional, technological and commercial measures to translate the Convention’s provisions into practical outcomes. The GSA also called on the media to help raise public awareness of the Convention and explain its implications for trade competitiveness, access to finance and the digitalisation of commercial processes. The Authority reaffirmed its commitment to working with relevant ministries, the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), industry stakeholders and international partners to promote awareness and support the Convention’s effective adoption and implementation. Professor Gyampo said modern, predictable and efficient trade documentation was essential to reducing avoidable costs and strengthening the competitiveness of Ghanaian businesses. The October 26 signing ceremony is expected to bring representatives of governments, international organisations and the global trading community to Accra. The GSA says the event should serve as a starting point for sustained efforts to establish a more efficient, secure and digitally enabled trading environment.

items.title: Relance de l’industrie textile: Le MEFPT et Domitexka Saloum scellent un partenariat stratégique
items.description: Le ministère de l’Emploi, de la Formation professionnelle et technique (MEFPT) et Domitexka Saloum ont signé, ce vendredi, à Kahone, dans la région de Kaolack, une convention de partenariat destinée à renforcer la formation aux métiers du textile. Financée à hauteur de 60 millions de francs CFA par le 3FPT, cette initiative ambitionne de contribuer à la relance de l’industrie textile nationale et à la création d’emplois. La relance de l’industrie textile sénégalaise passe par la valorisation du potentiel industriel local. C’est dans cette perspective que le ministre Idrissa Samb a scellé ce partenariat avec l’usine Domitexka Saloum. Le programme couvre cinq métiers à savoir la teinture, le tissage industriel, le tricotage, la filature et l’impression industrielle. « Cette signature traduit la volonté commune de faire de la formation professionnelle et technique un levier de développement industriel, de création d’emplois et de transformation économique », a déclaré le ministre. Il a précisé que la convention consolide un accompagnement déjà engagé par son département. Pour le PDG de Domitexka Saloum, Serigne Mboup, l’heure est aux actes. « Notre coton quitte le Sénégal sans que nous puissions en tirer pleinement profit. Il est temps que cela change », a-t-il souligné, insistant sur la nécessité d’offrir des perspectives professionnelles aux jeunes. Selon lui, la reprise de l’usine pourrait générer plus de 4 000 emplois directs. Mamadou THIAM (Correspondant)

items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has expressed optimism that the emergency waste evacuation exercise at the IRECOP site will be completed within the next one to two months. During an inspection of the site on Friday, October 16, 2026, the Minister observed significant progress, with accumulated waste heaps substantially reduced and some sections almost completely cleared. He commended the operators, drivers, supervisors and district coordinators for their dedication and commitment to the National Emergency Waste Evacuation Exercise. Mr Ayariga said the next phase would involve reclaiming the land and dredging the adjoining river to restore the free flow of water. He also renewed the government’s appeal to corporate institutions and private sector organisations to support the exercise, particularly the planned dredging works, which will require substantial financial and logistical resources. The exercise forms part of efforts to address accumulated waste and improve environmental sanitation at the site.

items.title: dLocal et Western Union élargissent leur partenariat aux paiements de transferts d’argent (payouts) au Cameroun
items.description: © PARTENAIRE Le Cameroun est le premier marché à bénéficier de cette extension, qui s'appuie sur le partenariat d'encaissement (collections) déjà en place entre les deux entreprises. dLocal, la plateforme de paiement de référence qui connecte les commerçants du monde entier aux marchés émergents, et Western Union, un leader mondial du transfert d'argent transfrontalier, ont annoncé l'extension de leur partenariat en Afrique aux décaissements (payouts). Cette extension vient compléter le travail d'encaissement que les deux entreprises mènent déjà ensemble : dLocal fournit la couche technologique et de connectivité, tandis que des partenaires locaux agréés exécutent les services de paiement et de décaissement concernés. L'expansion débutera par un corridor de décaissement opérationnel au Cameroun. Un parcours plus fiable, de bout en bout Ce nouveau chapitre du partenariat offre aux bénéficiaires de transferts d'argent sur les marchés africains un moyen plus rapide et plus fiable de recevoir des fonds, via les moyens de paiement locaux qu'ils utilisent déjà au quotidien. Au Cameroun, l'un des marchés les plus fragmentés de la région et fondé sur les portefeuilles électroniques, les bénéficiaires pourront recevoir leurs transferts directement dans les portefeuilles locaux pris en charge, par l'intermédiaire de partenaires de décaissement locaux opérant dans le cadre des réglementations locales applicables (opérateurs de réseaux mobiles ou institutions financières). Cela comble une lacune qui leur laissait jusqu'ici peu d'options fiables. La fiabilité sur laquelle les expéditeurs de transferts comptent déjà s'étend désormais jusqu'au bénéficiaire, créant un parcours unique et fiable de l'envoi à la réception. Cette extension renforce également les bases permettant à Western Union de s'appuyer sur un partenaire unique pour l'encaissement comme pour le décaissement, soutenant ainsi la croissance continue des corridors de transferts numériques sur les marchés émergents. « Chez Western Union, notre priorité est toujours de faire en sorte que nos clients reçoivent leur argent de manière fiable et fluide, où qu'ils se trouvent », a déclaré Mohamed Touhami El Ouazzani, Vice-Président régional et Responsable Afrique chez Western Union. « Étendre notre collaboration avec dLocal aux décaissements nous permet d'offrir cette même fiabilité côté réception, en commençant par des marchés comme le Cameroun. » « L'encaissement et le décaissement ont toujours été traités comme deux problèmes distincts », a déclaré Agustin Botta, Responsable EMEA chez dLocal. « Résoudre la moitié d'un transfert, c'est laisser la moitié du problème entière. Avec Western Union, nous travaillons ensemble à combler cet écart, en construisant un parcours plus cohérent de l'envoi à la réception. » dLocal construit l'infrastructure financière des marchés de demain, en connectant les grandes entreprises mondiales à des milliards de consommateurs des marchés émergents en Amérique latine, en Afrique, en Asie et au Moyen-Orient. Grâce à la plateforme « One dLocal », les entreprises peuvent accepter des paiements, effectuer des décaissements et régler des fonds à l'échelle mondiale, sans avoir à gérer des intégrations fragmentées ni des entités locales. Western Union s'engage à aider les personnes du monde entier qui aspirent à construire un avenir financier pour elles-mêmes, leurs proches et leurs communautés. Les institutions leaders du transfert d'argent transfrontalier et multidevises, des paiements et des services financiers numériques permettent aux consommateurs, aux entreprises, aux institutions financières et aux gouvernements, dans plus de 200 pays et territoires et plus de 130 devises, de se connecter à des milliards de comptes bancaires, des millions de portefeuilles électroniques et de cartes, ainsi qu'à un réseau mondial de centaines de milliers de points de vente. Au-delà du Cameroun À l'avenir, les deux entreprises envisagent d'étendre le décaissement à d'autres marchés africains, notamment le Nigeria, avec des virements bancaires et des portefeuilles électroniques, dans le cadre d'une volonté plus large de couvrir l'ensemble du parcours du transfert sur un plus grand nombre de marchés émergents. Les marchés émergents sont à un tournant pour les transferts d'argent, les bénéficiaires attendant de plus en plus, à la réception, la même rapidité et la même fiabilité que celles dont les expéditeurs ont l'habitude. La Banque mondiale estime que les flux de transferts d'argent vers l'Afrique subsaharienne ont atteint environ 57 milliards de dollars US en 2024, ce qui rappelle l'importance de ces fonds pour les ménages qui les attendent. dLocal et Western Union y voient une étape supplémentaire dans la construction de cette fiabilité, corridor après corridor. Cet article dLocal et Western Union élargissent leur partenariat aux paiements de transferts d'argent (payouts) au Cameroun est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
